title: Dropout voltage at 50mA load (Vin sweep toward Vout, DR-003/gf180 convention)
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's DRAFT "Dropout @ 50 mA" row (< 300mV, DRAFT stretch < 200mV) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch), using the DRAFT row's own cited method ("gf180's ss/125C/Vin~=Vout+dropout convention"): fix I_LOAD at 50mA (the row's own test point) and sweep Vin down toward Vout to find the Vin-Vout margin at which regulation is lost, rather than sweeping load current at a single ample Vin (that measures load regulation, a different DRAFT row). That row is DRAFT (issue #1 not yet ratified) -- the bound below cites it directly, not an invented final limit, and needs re-verification once #1 rules. Methodology fixed by issue #71 (superseding #18's original method): the deck sweeps VIN downward, from a comfortably-regulating value toward a value well below the 1.8V target, at a finer (20mV) resolution than #18's original 50mV; dropout_v is the Vin-Vout margin at the VIN where VOUT first falls (`.meas dc ... fall=1`) through 98% of the 1.8V target as VIN decreases -- the classic "regulation just lost" dropout definition -- not a fixed low-VIN endpoint (#18's method reported the pass device's residual V_sd well past dropout, overstating the gap; see #71's PR for the derivation and design/README.md's campaign section for the closed-loop screening that motivated the fix). vout_at_max_vin_v is a light-headroom regulation sanity check at the sweep's top (first-swept) end.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: meas dc dropout_vin_x find v(vin) when v(vout)=1.764 fall=1

measurements.name: dropout_v
measurements.note: Vin - Vout margin at the VIN where VOUT, swept downward from 3.63V toward 1.5V at 20mV resolution, first falls through 1.764V (98% of the 1.8V DRAFT output target, i.e. the -2% departure-from-regulation point -- classic dropout-voltage definition) with I_LOAD fixed at 50mA. `.meas dc ... fall=1` linearly interpolates between the two bracketing sweep points, so the reported VIN is not quantized to the 20mV grid. Fixed by issue #71 -- superseding #18's original `v(vin)[0] - v(vout)[0]` at a fixed low-VIN endpoint (1.9V), which measured deep past dropout rather than at the loss-of-regulation point (see #71 for the closed-loop screening that motivated this and design/README.md's campaign section for the corrected number). At -40C/27C this measurement is reliable (confirmed against independent per-point `.op` checks -- see the testbench schematic header). At 125C (all five process corners, not just the ff/sf thermal-shutdown false-trip #69 tracks) the underlying DC-solution-multiplicity #71 investigated is severe enough to corrupt this measurement at some corners (solver convergence failures, not real dropout numbers) -- read 125C dropout_v/vout_at_max_vin_v with the same caution already applied to ff/sf's 125C numbers, not as real measurements. Follow-up: #81. DRAFT bound: spec/target-spec.md "Dropout @ 50 mA" row, < 300mV (DRAFT stretch < 200mV, not applied here).

measurements.name: vout_at_max_vin_v
measurements.note: Vout at the sweep's first-swept (highest, 3.63V) VIN point -- ample headroom. A wide sanity-range check (not a tight spec bound) that regulation is at least in a sane operating range at the sweep's easiest point. Index 0 rather than a point-count-dependent index (#71): the sweep now runs VIN high-to-low, so the first point is always the sweep's highest VIN regardless of step size.
